newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: EU sees no change to Cairns Group agri-trade call.
newsitem.headline: EU sees no change to Cairns Group agri-trade call.

text.p: The European Union (EU) was not bracing for any unexpected challenges from the annual ministerial meetings of the Cairns Group of agricultural exporting countries in Rio de Janeiro on Thursday and Friday, the European Union's ambassador to Australia said on Wednesday.

The Australia-led group was expected to call for liberalisation of world agricultural markets as quickly as possible, Aneurin Rhys Hughes, EU ambassador and head of delegation to Australia and New Zealand, told Reuters from Canberra.
"There would be nothing new in our view from that," he said.
EU Foreign Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan last month called for complete world free trade negotiations by the new millenium, Hughes said.
The EU position remained for discussions on further liberalisation to take place to year 2000 agreed under the Marrakesh Accord in 1994, he said.
"I certainly don't expect anything new (in the Cairns Group meetings) beyond a reiteration of a commitment to further liberalisation," he said.
Asked about reports of continued Cairns Group concern over EU farm subsidies, Hughes said any concern would be misplaced, adding that it had removed most of its internal subsidies.
"You don't have any mountains of milk or lamb or lakes of wine any longer," he said.
A recent danger had arisen over a need to cut back on meat production to avoid problems in the future, he said.
But EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler was on record as saying that the EU hoped to be rid of all production subsidies by 2000, Hughes said.
Cairns Group officials were quoted from Rio de Janeiro on Tuesday as saying one of the group's main concerns was the high level of subsidies in the EU.
Hughes noted the Cairns Group now even had a European candidate for membership through Hungary.
Wendy Craik, executive director of Australia's National Farmers' Federation, said on Wednesday that Australian farm groups would favour a focus on greater liberalisation in the Cairns Group sessions.
A spokesman for Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said full details of the Australian government's position in the Cairns Group meetings would be released on Thursday.
